answer.summary: Ian McAllister defines working backwards as starting with a customer’s problem or goal, then finding an elegant solution to it—not beginning with a preferred product idea and retrofitting a problem. Amazon’s press release and FAQ are mechanisms to enforce that discipline, not the essence of the approach.

sections.heading: Start with the customer problem
sections.content: First establish what the team is trying to accomplish for the customer or business, and focus on the customer problem. Only then work toward a solution. Starting with something the team wants to build and adding a customer or problem afterward is not working backwards.

sections.heading: The press release and FAQ are tools
sections.content: Amazon used a press release and FAQ to help enforce the approach. McAllister describes writing a paragraph about the problem, then a solution paragraph and a customer quote; the FAQ asks whether there is a legitimate plan to succeed. The format is a useful mechanism, but teams can use other formats once they have built the habit of working from the problem to the solution.

sections.heading: When to use the process
sections.content: McAllister says the process has some overhead and may not make sense below a certain scale, but he considers it appropriate for a new product. The template is optional; remaining faithful to the customer problem is the important part.
